residual.wall: Textbook KV has E and η. Gasper only integrates τ=η/E. Inventing E and η sliders would fake two numbers from one ratio. Plant stiffness is an E-ratio, not a new dashpot.

question: Which Kelvin–Voigt parameters do we actually have, what do τ_plant=0.02 and viscoTau=0.25 mean as E and η, and what must never become a slider?
coordinateSpaces: Discrete Voigt creep in content px: x ← x+(x*−x)(1−e^{−dt/τ}). Exact for ẋ=(x*−x)/τ. τ seconds. Factory viscoTau=0.25. Floor 0.02. dt≈1/60 at 60 fps, 1/120 on 120 fps takes. No pascals. No mass in this integrator (CoM k,c is the other organ).
physicalLaw: Kelvin–Voigt: σ = E ε + η ε̇. Creep under constant stress: ε(t)=ε∞(1−e^{−t/τ}), τ=η/E. Our _lp is that ODE toward the posed shape x*.
We store one number: τ. We do not store E. We do not store η. E and η are not recoverable from τ alone.
If η is shared (one material, two contacts): τ_plant/τ_swing = E_swing/E_plant. 0.02/0.25 = 1/12.5. Plant is 12.5× stiffer than swing. That is the earned E-ratio.
If instead η dropped at the plant and E held: the plant would be less viscous, not more solid. Wrong picture for a floor. Gate E (via τ), not η.
Phase lag of a sinusoid at f: φ=atan(2π f τ). Strut ~1.43 Hz: swing τ=0.25 → φ≈66° (late). Plant τ=0.02 → φ≈10° (tracks). Weight 0.50 → φ≈77° (underwater).
D-0018 floor: at 60 fps, sa(0.02)≈0.565 still kills half a pixel-flip per frame. sa(0)=1 is a snap. sa(0.25)≈0.065 matches the authored ~15× first-frame cut.
CoM kX/kY/cLow/cHigh are not KV parameters. Do not fold them into E or η.
artisticLaw: Weight is τ_swing only. It is not E. It is not η. It is not settle.
Plant E-ratio is 12.5 and not a slider. The floor is a fact.
Do not offer an E slider and an η slider that multiply back into the same τ.
invariants: One live scalar: viscoTau. Range 0.02–1.0. Default 0.25.
Plant τ fixed at 0.02 when gated. Not 0. Not owner-tunable.
Do not add E, η, or ζ knobs to the rail.
Do not retune N37 c to chase a KV number.
